name: Olive mud
lede: Olive mud is a dark, brownish olive, closer to wet earth than to the fruit, and it shares its exact screen color with a second library name, Field Drab.

sections.title: Earth, not fruit
sections.body:
The library files Olive mud through the ISCC-NBS 1955 lists, which classify it as a moderate olive brown [1]. The name joins [[olive]] to [[mud]], landing on the brown, low-chroma end of the olive family rather than the green most people picture [1]. At this hex our library also records a second name, Field Drab, at an identical value, two different everyday words for the same dull brown [1].

The nearest distinct neighbor is [[acanthe|Acanthe]], about 2.6 units away by CIEDE2000, with [[mud-brown|Mud Brown]] close behind it [1]. In LCH terms it measures lightness 37, chroma 34, hue 84 degrees, Munsell 3.2Y 3.7/5.1 [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in 2,155 of 23,781 paintings, 9.06 percent, as photographed [2]. It is most over-represented in the 1440s, in 11 of that decade's 58 paintings, about twice the expected rate [2]. Fritz Thomsen is its most devoted painter here, carrying it in 11 of his 18 works, nearly 7 times the baseline [2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so a color match is not a pigment test [2].
